document.title: Gandhi Letter to Reagan
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Gandhi recalls U.S. welcome of India's active role, says India contacted groups in and outside Afghanistan, and warns of Gorbachev's forthcoming announcement that withdrawal begins May 15 and finishes in ten months.

events.description: Rajiv Gandhi visited Washington and held talks with Reagan.
Gandhi writes to Reagan reporting Gorbachev's message on Soviet troop withdrawal from Afghanistan.
Gorbachev via Vorontsov conveys willingness to begin withdrawal May 15 and complete within ten months, with about half of troops in first phase, if agreements are reached by March 15.
Official-level discussions between India and the Soviets on early Afghan withdrawal (late January).
Jayewardene visited India as Republic Day chief guest and discussed implementation of the Indo-Sri Lankan Agreement; handed over a draft treaty of peace and friendship.
Aid Sri Lanka Group met in Paris and agreed to contribute to reconstruction.
Gandhi visited Washington and held talks with Reagan.
Indian officials held discussions with Soviets at official level on Afghanistan withdrawal.

Gorbachev conveyed via Vorontsov that the USSR would begin withdrawal from Afghanistan on May 15 and complete within ten months, if agreements were reached by March 15; about half of troops to withdraw in the first phase.
Proposed start date of Soviet troop withdrawal from Afghanistan.
Target date for settlement agreements in the Geneva process.
Jayewardene visited India as Chief Guest at Republic Day celebrations and discussed the Indo-Sri Lankan Agreement.
Jayewardene handed over a draft treaty of peace and friendship between India and Sri Lanka.
Gandhi writes to Reagan on Afghanistan, Sri Lanka and the Soviet submarine lease.

key_claims: India had begun preliminary contacts with various groups within and outside Afghanistan at US suggestion, with nothing concrete yet.
The USSR told India it would begin withdrawing troops from Afghanistan on May 15, 1988 and finish within ten months if settlement agreements were reached by March 15.
Roughly half of Soviet troops would be withdrawn in the first phase.
India's stated objective is an independent, non-aligned Afghanistan free from outside interference.
India pressed the Soviets for a credible, phased withdrawal both during Ryzhkov's visit and at official level in January 1988.
